## CRG - Render Report PDF
Called by the main workflow via Execute Sub-workflow. Pure function: report data in, PDF binary out. Reusable for other report types since the HTML/PDF logic lives here, not in the main canvas.

## Binary file trick
Gotenberg's Chromium route requires a real multipart file part named with an .html filename — a plain text field is rejected. The Code node builds that binary manually (base64 + mimeType + fileName) so no Convert-to-File node or extra credential is needed here.

Retry: 3 attempts, 3s apart, 30s timeout — covers a Gotenberg cold start.

Option A: Self-hosted Gotenberg. No per-document cost, documents never leave your infrastructure. Requires Docker; works on self-hosted n8n only, not n8n Cloud. This is the default engine (Config.pdfEngine = gotenberg).

Option B: Hosted API (PDFShift). Works anywhere including n8n Cloud, no infrastructure to run. Per-document cost (free tier: 50 documents per month, no card required, then paid). Your HTML/data passes through a third party. Switch by setting Config.pdfEngine to api. Authenticated via an httpHeaderAuth credential (header name X-API-Key), never a hardcoded key.

STATUS: fully built and configured, but NOT yet tested with a real PDFShift account -- no credential exists in the reference instance this was built and tested in.

Two failure layers: (1) if the credential is entirely missing/unbound, n8n rejects the run before this node executes at all -- CRG - Error Alert detects that specific case and rewrites the alert into a plain-language message telling you to add the credential. (2) if a credential IS configured but the call still fails (expired key, PDFShift outage, rate limit), THAT is a normal node error, caught here by Format PDFShift Failure / Fail - PDF API Engine Error with the same kind of clear message.
